theme: Save, O LORD, the tongue and its lying words
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 12. It is a short prayer of David about a world full of lies. Notice the contrast between the words of the wicked and the words of the LORD.
settingTheScene: Psalm 12 is a psalm of David, “according to The Sheminith,” possibly a musical direction. David prays in a time when truth seems to have vanished, when flattery and boasting fill the land and the poor are trampled. It fits our reading in James, where the tongue can be a fire or a source of blessing, and teaches what to do when the words around us cannot be trusted.
observation: “Save, O LORD, for the godly one is gone; for the faithful have vanished from among the children of man” (v. 1).
“Everyone utters lies to his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak” (v. 2).
“May the LORD cut off all flattering lips” (v. 3).
“Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, I will now arise” (v. 5).
“The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace on the ground, purified seven times” (v. 6).
“You, O LORD, will keep them; you will guard us from this generation forever” (v. 7).
“On every side the wicked prowl, as vileness is exalted among the children of man” (v. 8).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a cry of alarm: “Save, O LORD, for the godly one is gone; for the faithful have vanished from among the children of man!” David feels that no honest person remains. The problem is speech: “Everyone utters lies to his neighbor; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.” The phrase “a double heart” is literally “a heart and a heart”: saying one thing and meaning another. This is the same double-mindedness James warns about. David asks God to cut off flattering lips and the boastful tongue, those who say, “With our tongue we will prevail, our lips are with us; who is master over us?” They believe their words are their own and answer to no one.

Then the LORD speaks, and the psalm turns: “Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, I will now arise,” says the LORD; “I will place him in the safety for which he longs.” God hears the groaning of the needy and responds with a promise. Where human words are lies, his words can be trusted: “The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace on the ground, purified seven times.” Silver purified seven times has no impurity. We can rest our whole weight on what God says.

The psalm ends with confidence mixed with realism. “You, O LORD, will keep them; you will guard us from this generation forever.” The promise is of protection, not of an easy time: “On every side the wicked prowl, as vileness is exalted among the children of man.” The wicked still prowl, and shame is honored. But the word of the LORD stands. This is the experience of the church in every age. Evil seems to be flourishing, yet God’s words are pure, and God keeps his own. In Christ, the Word who is the truth (John 14:6), we find the final answer. The one who “committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth” (1 Peter 2:22) is the faithful one in a world of liars.
connection: James 3:1-12 speaks of the tongue. Psalm 5:9 and 55:21 describe flattering and deceitful speech. Psalm 119:140 and Proverbs 30:5 describe the purity of God’s word. Isaiah 3:14-15 speaks of the plundered poor. Exodus 3:7-8 shows God hearing the groaning of the oppressed. Isaiah 33:10 has a similar “now I will arise.” John 14:6 and 17:17 present Jesus and the word as truth. 1 Peter 2:22 speaks of Christ’s speech. Ephesians 4:25 commands truth-telling. Revelation 21:8 and 22:15 speak of the end of liars.
application:
Make yourself a person of single-hearted speech today: say what you mean, and refuse flattery.

When you feel that truth has vanished around you, turn to Scripture as pure silver and read a passage slowly.

Pray for the poor and needy in your community, and ask what the LORD may want you to do.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what lies and flattery you see.
Thank him that his words are pure.
Ask him to keep you from boasting and double speech.
